summary: Italian poet and celebrity Gabriele D'Annunzio raped servant women, agitated Italy into World War I in 1915 and seized Fiume in 1919, ruling it as a dictator with rituals and a salute later copied by Mussolini's fascists.

evidence.note: rape of a peasant girl and lifelong pattern of raping servant women
runs for parliament in 1897, serves one term
flees debts to Paris in 1910, then visits the Reims front
1914 Reims article starts his push for Italian intervention
Italy declares war in May 1915 after his Rome speeches
attached to the Third Army; bombing and leaflet raids
marches on Fiume with Arditi in September 1919 and seizes it
sets up a press office to send communiques worldwide
Italian siege ends his rule of Fiume in January 1921

notes: main_span 1914-1921 (interventionism to Fiume); poetry fame from 1879 could argue an earlier start. Transcript dates differ from known facts: L'Innocente given as 1882 (1892), Fiume plebiscite as 1916 (1920). Mussolini gets no standalone segment so is a keyword. No polity id for the Kingdom of Italy. themes.yaml lists this episode under fascism-far-right as 'Mussolini', though the subject is D'Annunzio.
